subject.title: Model safety/alignment can block explicitly authorized operational tasks (e.g. SSH diagnostics)

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted-operator diagnostics/refusal contract for explicitly authorized read-only infrastructure tasks, and where should that boundary live?
rationale: The remaining work changes the product and security contract between model safety behavior, operator authority, tool policy, exec approvals, and provider refusals; code inspection cannot choose that policy safely.

options.title: Define a narrow diagnostics contract
options.body: Keep the current security gates, add explicit model/auth-policy/tool-failure observability, and only relax execution guidance for authorized read-only diagnostics inside that contract.

options.title: Limit scope to provider refusals
options.body: Let the narrower provider-refusal fallback issues handle classifier false positives and leave broader SSH/admin soft-refusal behavior unchanged for now.

options.title: Do not add core behavior
options.body: Document current trusted-operator expectations and require users to use direct tool invocation, trace raw, or manual diagnostics when model behavior is too cautious.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow diagnostics contract
recommendation.body: Keep the current security gates, add explicit model/auth-policy/tool-failure observability, and only relax execution guidance for authorized read-only diagnostics inside that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent related Anthropic refusal fallback work and security-boundary discussion make steipete the clearest available decision owner from the inspected history.
